newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan plans business mission to N.Korea - papers.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan plans business mission to N.Korea - papers.

text.p: A semi-official Taiwan business delegation will visit North Korea to negotiate mutual trade offices, direct air links and other sensitive issues, local newspapers said on Monday.
Such a visit would almost certainly irk South Korea, a long-time enemy of North Korea, as well as communist China, Taiwan's rival after the Chinese civil war split them in 1949.

The 50-strong delegation comprising officials and enterprise leaders from the Nationalist Party, private Far Eastern Air Transport and other companies planned to leave for Pyongyang in April, the newspapers reported.
Liu Tai-ying, who as head of the ruling Nationalists' business management committee presides over some US$1.4 billion in party assets, was scheduled to lead the mission, they said.
Committee spokeswoman Grace Fang flatly denied that Liu was leading such a delegation, but could not comment on whether a trip was taking place.
"He has no plan to visit. I don't know where it came from," she said of the report.
Fang acknowledged that the Nationalist Party already had sent Liang Lun-ke, chairman of party-run Yu Tai Enterprise, to North Korea to discuss problems with a 1996 barter trade deal.

North Korea's de facto representative, Yang Chih-fang of Pyongyang-run Korean International Travel, told Reuters that North Korea hoped to open a trade office with a visa function in Taipei but declined to comment on Monday's report.

The Commercial Times quoted unnamed officials as saying the group hoped to negotiate direct flights between Taipei and Pyongyang and the opening of a North Korean trade office in Taipei to handle visas, trade issues and other business.
The group will discuss expanding barter trade with North Korea and boosting Taiwan's investments there, the paper said.

The report said Taipei wanted to improve relations with North Korea despite what officials regarded as South Korea's "unfriendly" protests over Taiwan's plans to ship low-level nuclear waste to North Korea for disposal.

For decades, South Korea was Taiwan's top Asian ally due to their common opposition to communist China and its reclusive Stalinist ally North Korea. The alliance collapsed after Seoul stunned Taipei by switching official ties to Beijing in 1992.
Seoul has loudly protested against Taiwan's nuclear waste plan, saying it would pollute the Korean peninsula.
Taipei has countered that the low-radiation waste -- mainly contaminated clothes and helmets -- would be handled under international safeguards and posed no risk.

As for the sour trade deal, sources said Nationalist-owned firm Yu Tai had struck a barter deal in 1996 and sent some T$1 billion (US$36 million) worth of rice and daily necessity items to North Korea in exchange for raw materials.
North Korea failed to ship the materials to Taiwan due to serious flooding that Pyongyang said wiped out a good part of the country's harvest, the sources said.
